Verified all switch mappings, interrupt restoration, the assertion preceding initialization of format, and the absent default. Build-dependent assertion evaluation is appropriately qualified.
Verified HSD's selected-XFB calls, alignment assertion, protected pointer storage, conditional right-base refresh, collective conversion, flush snapshot, and field-dependent retrace commit.
The void function exits its sleep loop when retraceCount changes, restores interrupts, and completes normally.
Canonical implementation uses mode & 2 and mode >> 2 with full-mode timing selection and terminal special cases. Header definitions distinguish non-interlace 1 from progressive 2.
Right calculation and staging are guarded by threeD, but the collective threshold expression and four shifts are not. Existing right storage can consequently be consumed and mutated outside 3D.
Verified the five staged vertical registers and all four cited callers: configure and adjustment pass adjusted height; pan and black pass DispSizeY.

contradictions.reason: Accepted deferral of both compiled-section claims: declarations establish storage roles, not exact section membership, extents, or padding; dbgCount is additionally DEBUG-dependent. Supported source-level knowledge remains retained.
Both VIInit supersessions are justified: only horizontal adjustment is imported, and software black initialization is distinct from forcing enabled hardware black.
The VIGetTvFormat correction preserves supported mappings while explicitly recording an indeterminate assertion operand and unsupported-mode return path.
Both framebuffer supersessions correctly distinguish conditionally refreshed right addresses from collectively consumed representation state; flush is not immediate hardware application.
Non-returning was an incorrect classification of VIWaitForRetrace; normal completion is explicit.
The low-level initializer's literal mask cannot be normalized to the ordinary non-interlace flag; the proposed numeric distinction is supported.
The always-adjusted-height claim is contradicted by pan and black callers. The replacement preserves caller-specific representations.

Accepted deferral of all three broader PAL retail claims. Timing profiles and platform setup do not establish retail menu toggles or progressive tests. EURGB60 consumer behavior is not uniform: PAD rejects it, GX takes its assertion/fallback path, and HSD assigns non-NTSC a nominal period of 50.

The functionality document correctly preserves the cross-file lifetime distinction: deferred VI commit does not suppress the later post-callback, and successful publication uses live HorVer. HSD ownership advancement must not be equated with guaranteed same-retrace hardware completion.
